original_value: This study reviews the technique of convolutional neural network (CNN) applied in a specific field of mammographic breast cancer diagnosis (MBCD). It aims to provide several clues on how to use CNN for related tasks. MBCD is a long-standing problem, and massive computer-aided diagnosis models have been proposed. The models of CNN-based MBCD can be broadly categorized into three groups. One is to design shallow or to modify existing models to decrease the time cost as well as the number of instances for training; another is to make the best use of a pretrained CNN by transfer learning and fine-tuning; the third is to take advantage of CNN models for feature extraction, and the differentiation of malignant lesions from benign ones is fulfilled by using machine learning classifiers. This study enrolls peer-reviewed journal publications and presents technical details and pros and cons of each model. Furthermore, the findings, challenges and limitations are summarized and some clues on the future work are also given. Conclusively, CNN-based MBCD is at its early stage, and there is still a long way ahead in achieving the ultimate goal of using deep learning tools to facilitate clinical practice. This review benefits scientific researchers, industrial engineers, and those who are devoted to intelligent cancer diagnosis.

result.paraphrase: This review examines convolutional neural network (CNN) techniques applied to mammographic breast cancer diagnosis (MBCD), with the goal of offering guidance on using CNN for related tasks. Because MBCD is a long-standing problem and many computer-aided diagnosis models have been proposed, CNN-based MBCD models are generally divided into three categories: designing shallow or modified models to reduce training time and the number of training instances; leveraging pretrained CNNs through transfer learning and fine-tuning; and using CNNs for feature extraction, followed by machine-learning classifiers to distinguish malignant lesions from benign ones. The study includes peer-reviewed journal articles and outlines the technical details, advantages, and disadvantages of each approach. It also summarizes the findings, challenges, and limitations, while suggesting directions for future work. Overall, CNN-based MBCD remains in an early stage, and considerable progress is still needed before deep learning tools can fully support clinical practice. This review is useful for scientific researchers, industrial engineers, and others working on intelligent cancer diagnosis.
